title: How do we draw the letter Y with given angles?
description: The three angles at the junction of the letter Y fill a full turn of three hundred sixty degrees. Taking the upper sixty away leaves three hundred, which splits into two equal angles of one hundred fifty degrees.
teaching_notes: One idea: the angles round a point fill three hundred sixty degrees, so equal angles share what is left. Watch for students who draw the stem to make one hundred fifty degrees on the same side as the V.

video_script.why: The child draws the upper V of sixty degrees, then uses the full turn to see that each of the other two angles is one hundred fifty degrees.
video_script.substitution: Draw 60 degrees for the top V, take 60 from 360 to get 300, then half of 300 is 150 for each side angle.
video_script.anchor: an empty board with a protractor and a ruler
video_script.payoff_line: The whole turn gives the two equal side angles

final_answer.value: the letter Y with 150°, 60° and 150° at the junction
final_answer.spoken: the letter Y has angles of one hundred fifty, sixty and one hundred fifty degrees at its junction

never_show: a stem drawn so that the 150° angle is on the same side as the V
maths_rules: the two side angles are equal, so each is 300° ÷ 2 = 150°
video_script.design: One board. The upper V is teal, the two side angles are amber, and the protractor is placed at the junction with its zero line along one arm.

narration: <bookmark mark='equal'/>Step three, the two side angles are equal.

<bookmark mark='mark'/>Mark one hundred fifty degrees on the side away from the V.
<bookmark mark='stem'/>Draw the stem of the Y down through that mark.
